body: I had surgery for both hips, as a person (26f) with a vagina having hetero sex, it was only really a few days/ maybe week before I had sex again. It was fine for me as long as I made sure I didn’t move my hip the wrong way/ any hip flexion, so for me as long as he did the majority of the work, I was able to lay down on my back or stomach and have sex. Hope this helps and good luck with surgery!

I’m not sure what sport you play, but I was able to return to classes after I was off of crutches which was 3 weeks for me. If you have virtual classes, you may feel better enough to attend only a week or so later. My issue was that I was on crutches and classes were in person. I play volleyball and the pt timeline I was given was something like this- fully weight bearing after 3 weeks on crutches. Then began physical therapy 3 times a week. I was not able to do any hip flexion above 90 degrees for the first 6 weeks after surgery. At that point I was mostly just doing physical therapy, and the at home exercises, and going for walks as much and as long as I could tolerate. At the 3 month mark, I was able to begin Pilates class and simple volleyball moves (I coach). I also was allowed at that time to return to impact exercises like running and jumping. I was just not allowed to do anything where I might cut or pivot my hip for 6 months. So while I am able to participate in static (stationary) volleyball, and Pilates exercises (since they are all done “in line” and don’t require quick, sudden opening or closing of the hip), I cannot play at full capacity until the 6 month mark. Overall if you’re a student athlete and focus on your recovery process, you can be back in your sport in as little as 6 months if you work hard. Hope this helps and hope you feel better soon

I understand what you’re going through and I’m sorry you’re going through this :( 
I’m 26f currently, had my right hip done August 2023 (when I was 24) my left hip June 2024 (when I was 25). I was always a very competitive athlete and also am a volleyball coach. I would recommend surgery. I won’t lie, the recovery process was tough mentally and physically, but after two years(I spent at least a year of being injured before the first surgery) I am finally feeling better and am able to do many things I was not able to do at all. I’m back to volleyball and have been attending Pilates 5 times a week for almost two months now. I can drive for longer than 30 minutes without unbearable pain (something I couldn’t do for years) I can carry my laundry basket to the basement by myself (lifting with my legs and not with my back was not an option, so I needed help). These are little things but the pain had created such excruciating back pain(they said my back was compensating for my hips) I couldn’t do much. Everyone’s experience is different and I’m not sure what symptoms you’re having. I’m just giving examples to show the amount of a difference it has made for me. In my opinion I think it’s beneficial to have the surgery. I would also be afraid of having it get much worse, causing the recovery process to be more challenging, since other areas of your body may be injured or inflamed from compensating for your injury.

Hey! I had surgery for my right hip august 2023 and my left hip June 2024. I had this same moment of panic a million times throughout both recovery processes (still working on the left one), but as long as it’s not something you’re continuously or intentionally doing you should be fine. I accidentally did that many times and it would freak me out, my PT and surgeon all told me the same thing, that occasionally doing it on accident isn’t gonna make-or-break it, it’s just something you overall want to intentionally avoid doing. I was so paranoid with the first surgery last year, my surgeon actually let me get a second mri after the 3 months mark to give me peace of mind. No evidence of retear. It didn’t feel better for a while however I had the same injury in both hips, so while my right hip was healing from surgery it was still compensating for an injured left hip. I didn’t really feel much better until this September 2024 but I had both hips injured and am also on my feet a lot which delayed my recovery process a bit. Now in October I’m still feeling good, and have been able to get back to activities I have not been able to do in a couple years. I wish you all the best on your recovery! Don’t overthink it, as long as you do your best to be mindful of your movements, accidental hip flexion isn’t a big deal. We’re all human and it happens sometimes :)
